sentences.text:
Author: Battu Devanand
Bench: Battu Devanand
 The Honourable Sri Justice Battu Devanand
 Contempt Case No.606 Of 2018
1. This Contempt Case has been filed complaining willful
disobedience in implementing the Order dated 14.12.2017 passed
by this Court in W.P.No.42563 of 2017.

2.  The petitioners filed W.P.No.42563 of 2017 aggrieved by the action of the respondents in laying the road through their land,
without following procedure and without paying compensation under the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition and Resettlement Act, 2013.
3.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: This Court disposed of the said W.P.No.42563 of 2017 on 14.12.2017, directing the respondents not to interfere with the possession of the petitioners over the subject land without following the due process of law.
4. The Respondent Nos.1 & 2 filed separate counter affidavits stating that, the petitioners are the absolute owners of land of an extent of Ac.0-72 cents in Sy.No.64/1.

During inspection of the land in question by the Tahsildar, Ramakuppam and Panchayat DEV,J Raj officials on 28.03.2018, the petitioners have apportioned land of an extent of Ac.0-06 cents in Sy.No.64/1 for formation of road,
without claiming any compensation and also consented to withdraw the cases filed by them before the concerned Courts.
The petitioners were granted Ac.0-03 cents each in Sy.No.577 of Bandarlapalle Village, for compensating their land of Ac.0-06 cents to the Government for formation of road.

It is submitted that, inspite of grant of land equal to the extent said to have been lost by the petitioners, they have again filed contempt case with malafide intention to claim undue benefits from the Government.

5. Respondent No.2 filed additional affidavit, stating that the petitioners are continuing in enjoyment of the land since the date of grant of house site patta in Sy.No.577/7C of Bandarlapalle-I Village of Ramakuppam Mandal, as such, there is no willful, intentional, deliberate violation of the order passed by this Court and requested to close the contempt case.

sentences.text: Respondent No.3 - Executive Engineer, Panchayat Raj Department, filed counter affidavit denying material allegations and he submitted the information secured from Respondent Nos.1 & 2.

Further, he stated that, he is not the competent authority to DEV,J initiate any land acquisition proceedings and being an Executive Engineer, his duty is only to execute engineering works, as sanctioned and directed by the Government, as such, requested to close the contempt case against him.
7.

Heard Sri C. Prakash, learned counsel for the petitioners, and Sri T.V.S. Kumar, learned counsel for the Respondent Nos.1 & 2 and Sri Kiran Kumar Vadlamudi, learned counsel for Respondent No.3 and perused the material available on record.

8. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that, though the respondents received and acknowledged the order passed by this Hon'ble Court on 14.12.2017, the respondents did not comply with the Orders of this Court in true spirit.
They highhandedly interfered with the petitioners land and laid the road during the period 06.01.2018 to 08.01.2018 without following the procedure and without paying compensation.
9. Learned counsel submits that the respondents deliberately flouted the orders of this Court.

The failure on the part of the respondent in implementing the orders of this Court would amount to disobedience of the orders of this Hon'ble Court, and, DEV,J therefore, they are liable for punishment under Sections 10 to 12 of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971.
Complaining the same, the petitioner filed the present Contempt Case.
10. Sri K. Chidambaram, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the respondents submits that the order of the Court is complied with by providing alternative land to the petitioners to compensate them.
He further submitted that, admittedly there is some delay in implementing the order of the Court in true spirit.
But, the delay caused is neither wilful nor wanton.

Learned Senior Counsel requested that, as already the petitioners are compensated, the Court may be pleased to close the contempt case by accepting the unconditional apology tendered by the respondents by taking a lenient view with regard to the delay.

11. Having heard the submissions of the respective counsel and upon perusal of the material available on record, it appears that the land in Sy.No.64/1 with an extent of Ac.0-72 cents is recorded in the names of the petitioners in the village accounts of Ramakuppam Village in Ramakuppam Mandal.
Pattadar passbooks and title deeds have been issued to them for the said land vide Khata No.611 and 516 respectively.
There is a road with DEV,J 10 feet covering an extent of Ac.0-04 cents passing through the field as per Village plan since 60 years.
The said road is developed as Black Top (BT) Road in connection with the visit of Hon'ble Chief Minister of A.P on 09.01.2018.
While laying the BT Road, the Panchayat Authorities have laid the road over an extent of Ac.0-10 cents.

After negotiations took place before the elders of the village and for the purpose of compensating the petitioners for the land of Ac.0-10 cents wherein, the Panchayat Raj authorities laid road, the Tahsildar has granted house site pattas in the names of the wives of the petitioners to an extent of Ac.0-03 cents in Sy.No.577 of Bandarlapalle Village in the year 2018, vide VHS No.672/1427 dated 28.06.2018.

But the possession of the land is not handed over to the petitioners P.V.Shiva Shankar vs P S Pradyumna I.A.S. on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4930043/
2 and their names were not entered into the revenue records.

sentences.text:
12. This case went several adjournments for conducting survey and filing additional documents etc.,
as per the requests of both side counsels.

13. The Respondent No.1 filed an affidavit on 10.03.2023 wherein, it is extracted as stated hereinunder:
DEV,J "2.

It is submitted that, orders were issued by the Collector, Chittoor vide D.Dis.L7/e-391975/22 dated 07.03.2023 to the Tahsildar, Ramakuppam, according permission for exchange of Govt. lands in Sy.No.577/10 extent Ac.0-04 cents and Sy.577/11 extent Ac.0-04 cents of Bandarlapalle revenue village in lieu of the patta lands in Sy.No.64/1 Ac.0-10 cents lost by the writ petitioners for formation of BT Road, for agricultural purposes as agreed by the petitioners.

3. It is submitted that, necessary mutations were also done in weland adangal effecting changes in favour of the writ petitioners for the lands in Sy.No.577/10 extent Ac.0-04 cents and Sy.No.577/11 extent Ac.0-04 cents of Bandarlapalle Revenue Village which were allotted to the writ petitioners in exchange of their lands."
14.

On careful perusal of the entire material available on record, and in view of the facts and circumstances and in the light of the affidavit filed by Respondent No.1 on 10.03.2023, it is established that the petitioners are compensated by allotting government land to an extent of Ac.0-04 cents each in Sy.No.577/10 and Sy.No.577/11, in lieu of the patta lands of Ac.0-10 cents lost by them for formation of BT Road.
DEV,J 15.
It is an admitted fact that, there is a delay in compensating the petitioners by the respondents.

16. The Respondent No.1 submits that, he instructed his subordinate officers in the year 2018 itself to allot land to the petitioners and accordingly, the concerned Tahsildar allotted Ac.0-03 cents of land each to the wives of the petitioners.
But, thereafter, he is under the impression that the land was handed over to the petitioners and no further litigation is pending.
The Respondent No.1 who appeared before this Court in-person, tendered his unconditional apology for the delay caused in implementing the order of this Court.
17. The Respondent Nos.2 & 3 also tendered their unconditional apologies in their affidavits.
18. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, in the considered opinion of this Court, the apology tendered by the respondents is bonafide and to be accepted.
19. For the reasons stated above, in the opinion of this Court, there is no wilful disobedience on the part of the respondents in implementing the order of this Court.
